summary: ARTales has a strong visual direction, several usable logo candidates and approved context materials. It is not ready for a locked Visual Identity Pack v1 because vector masters, transparent exports, final logo variant decisions, final color role confirmation, typography decisions and export profiles are still missing.

visualReferences.name: New logo.zip
visualReferences.notes: Contains one logo board and eight raster JPG logo/mark/monogram variants. These are useful for evaluation and selection, but are not production masters.

contextReferences.assessment: Strong brand context for care, calm, curation, trust and living culture.

candidatePolicy.notes: Non-selected candidates should remain available until the identity has been tested in real web, favicon, mobile, social and dark/light contexts.

wordmark.candidateAssessment: The ARTales wordmark is visually coherent and suitable as the core signature. The serif tone supports cultural dignity and calm. It still needs a final primary variant decision and vector preparation.
risks: Raster source can blur or degrade in production uses.
Some wordmark variants may lose legibility at small sizes.
Without a selected primary variant, future web/token work may drift.
wordmark.recommendation: Keep the strongest standalone wordmark as a primary candidate and test it in header, footer, brand sheet and social preview contexts before locking.

logoLockup.candidateAssessment: The symbol plus ARTales lockup is the strongest candidate for a public brand signature. It connects the literary mark with the name, works emotionally, and matches the dark/gold ARTales atmosphere. Several variants should be retained for testing.
risks: The symbol may be too detailed for very small header or social sizes.
Spacing and proportions may vary between raster variants unless rebuilt as a vector master.
Gold-on-dark works strongly, but gold-on-light needs contrast testing.
logoLockup.recommendation: Select 2-3 lockup candidates for real-context preview testing before locking one primary and one reserve variant.

symbol.candidateAssessment: The pen/drop/leaf-like symbol is distinctive and well aligned with literature, care and cultural craft. It is a strong candidate for mark/icon usage, but detail density must be tested at favicon and small avatar sizes.
risks: Internal detail may disappear at small sizes.
The symbol may need a simplified small-size version rather than one universal master.
symbol.recommendation: Keep as a primary symbol candidate. Prepare or request vector reconstruction and test whether a simplified favicon variant is needed.

monogram.candidateAssessment: The AT monogram is useful as a secondary or reserve mark, especially where the symbol is too detailed. It may read as more classic/luxury than literary-gallery, so it needs context testing before becoming a primary mark.
risks: Could compete with the pen/drop symbol if both are used without hierarchy.
May shift the tone toward luxury branding rather than calm cultural space.
monogram.recommendation: Retain as reserve candidate for avatar, seal or special-use contexts. Do not discard; do not make primary without comparison testing against the symbol.

availableInputs: working palette from visual manual and prior decisions
colorPalette.candidateAssessment: The dark ink, paper and muted gold direction is coherent with ARTales. The gold should function as accent/light, not as a large decorative surface. Values need formal confirmation and contrast checks before being locked as tokens.
risks: Gold can fail contrast for small text if used casually.
Too much gold could make the interface feel decorative or commercial instead of calm.
colorPalette.recommendation: Confirm semantic roles before tokenization: background, surface, text, muted text, accent, border, focus, state colors.

typography.candidateAssessment: The brand documents define the importance and tone of typography, but do not yet lock production fonts for headings, body text and UI. This is a blocker before serious tokenization.
risks: A mismatched type stack can undermine the calm literary tone even if logo and colors are strong.
Licensed fonts must not be used without clear rights.
typography.recommendation: Define 2-3 typography candidates and test them on homepage, work detail, reader-adjacent UI and long descriptive text.

graphicMotifs.candidateAssessment: The visual language has coherent metaphors: ink, paper, light, space, literary craft. These should become usage rules, not random decoration.
risks: Decorative motifs can easily create visual noise if not constrained.
AI-generated visuals should not become masters without review and provenance.
graphicMotifs.recommendation: Keep motifs as context/reference. Define permitted usage after logo/color/typography decisions.

backgroundsAndTextures.candidateAssessment: The dark textured surface and cream paper background support the gallery/literary mood, but production UI needs restrained rules and accessible contrast.
risks: Texture can reduce readability or make UI feel heavy.
Raster textures can increase web weight if used carelessly.
backgroundsAndTextures.recommendation: Treat textures as mood/reference until the tokenized UI has basic calm contrast without them.

exportProfiles.candidateAssessment: Export needs are known conceptually, but no final profiles exist yet because masters are not locked.
risks: Generating exports before masters are locked creates cleanup and drift.
Different social/web crops may reveal weaknesses in candidates.
exportProfiles.recommendation: Define profiles after selecting primary candidates, before creating final exports.

brandSheet.candidateAssessment: The existing logo board is useful as a visual reference, but not yet a final brand sheet because inputs are not locked and rules are incomplete.
risks: A polished brand sheet can falsely imply that the identity is already locked.
brandSheet.recommendation: Create a candidate comparison board first; create final brand sheet only after Visual Identity Pack v1 approval.

approval.recommendation: Move next to candidate comparison and missing master plan, not to production tokenization yet.

nextRecommendedSteps: Create a candidate comparison brief for wordmark, lockup, symbol and monogram.
Choose a primary candidate and reserve candidate for each logo role, without deleting rejected candidates.
Prepare or request SVG vector masters for selected candidates.
Define typography candidates and test them in real ARTales contexts.
Confirm semantic color roles and accessibility constraints.
Only then prepare Visual Identity Pack v1 exports and token skeleton.
